result.summary: Do not ship: two paths bypass discard confirmation. Reviewed pushed commit 8254d0d against master through GitHub; local runners failed, so tests were not rerun.

findings.title: The baseline can absorb unsaved edits made before hydration
findings.body: ProjectForm renders enabled, uncontrolled inputs before hydration, but this effect snapshots their live values only after ready becomes true. With delayed JavaScript, a user can enter project details first; those edits become the supposedly clean baseline. Cancel then leaves without warning unless another field changes. React preserves these input values during hydration ([React 19.2.3 source](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/v19.2.3/packages/react-dom-bindings/src/client/ReactDOMInput.js#L229-L259)).
findings.recommendation: Derive the baseline from original defaults, or prevent editing from server render until a pristine baseline is captured. Add a browser regression that enters project details before hydration, then presses Cancel.

findings.title: Pending photo attachments are invisible to the discard check
findings.body: On an otherwise unchanged NDOT or Waterways form, select photos and press Cancel while compression/upload is pending. PhotoAttachment updates the hidden JSON only after the upload batch finishes; its file input has no name and is disabled during upload. The snapshot therefore still matches, and server-action pending remains false. This branch navigates without confirmation, abandoning the attachment draft and potentially leaving uploaded files unreferenced.
findings.recommendation: Expose pending attachment work to FormCancel and require confirmation whenever it exists, or disable Cancel until uploads settle. FormData equality alone cannot establish that nothing will be lost.

next_steps: Fix both gaps and add browser regressions with delayed hydration and delayed photo uploads.
Verify Keep editing preserves values and attachment work, including after a rejected submission.
